subtitle: Ch. 8 — Ideal Gas Law, Molar Mass, Density & Gas Stoichiometry

questions.q: The ideal gas law equation is an approximation of a more complicated equation. It has the best results for molecules that are at low pressure and high temperature.
questions.note: True. At low pressure the molecules are far apart (their volume matters less) and at high temperature they move fast enough that attractions matter less.

questions.q: Gases do not obey the ideal gas law perfectly because the gas particles do interact and they also do occupy a small portion of the volume of the container.
questions.note: True. Those are exactly the two assumptions of the ideal gas model that real gases break.

questions.q: At STP, this reaction occurred: XY (g) + 3 AB (aq) → A₃Y (g) + B₃X (s). How many liters of gas are produced from 2.6 grams of AB?
questions.note: 2.6 g AB × (1 mol / 58.21 g) × (1 mol A₃Y / 3 mol AB) × (22.4 L / 1 mol) = 0.33 L. The only gas PRODUCT is A₃Y.
questions.given: You may or may not need all of this: molar mass AB = 58.21 g/mol · correct sig figs and unit.

questions.q: A gas phase reaction at constant temperature and pressure in a flexible container: A₂Z (g) + 2 X (g) → 2 AX (g) + Z (g). If 2.29 L of A₂Z react with excess X, how many liters of AX will form?
questions.note: When everything is a gas at the same T and P, volumes follow the mole ratio: 2.29 L A₂Z × (2 L AX / 1 L A₂Z) = 4.58 L.
